text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen nearly 19% over two weeks, with today's modest 1.2% decline continuing a sharp downturn that accelerated after the company's quarterly earnings report on November 3rd. The bigger story is the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections, which spooked refinery investors—a Democratic Congress is expected to push harder on renewable energy and climate policy, a headwind for traditional oil refiners. Meanwhile, U.S. crude has softened to $99.64 per barrel (down from levels that would have supported refiner margins), and refineries are running at 94.5% capacity, limiting upside from tight supply.

The political shift is the main weight on the stock: renewable energy policies that gain traction under Democratic control could erode long-term demand for refined products, even though near-term refining fundamentals (oil storage at 691 million barrels, gasoline inventory at 208 million) remain reasonable. Geopolitical risk—rising Iran tensions—could support oil prices if conflict escalates, but that's an uncertain offset to the structural headwind the election created for fossil-fuel refiners.
